summary: GPT-5 mini has no dedicated OpenAI system card, so this digest uses the GPT-5 System Card's `gpt-5-thinking-mini` evidence and labels family-level safeguards separately. The mini-specific evidence includes appendix safety tables, HealthBench, SimpleQA, Cyber Range, and SWE-bench statements, while larger GPT-5 Thinking and GPT-5 main results are not attributed to mini.

capabilities.text: The card identifies `gpt-5-thinking-mini` as the mini version of the thinking model and maps it as the successor path from OpenAI o4-mini.
OpenAI says reasoning models including `gpt-5-thinking-mini` are trained to deliberate before answering, revise strategies, and follow policy guidance.
`gpt-5-thinking-mini` scores 64.1% on HealthBench, 40.3% on HealthBench Hard, and 96.5% on HealthBench Consensus.
The model improves over prior releases on Cyber Range, including two unaided Simple Privilege Escalation solves and stronger hinted performance.
OpenAI says `gpt-5-thinking` and `gpt-5-thinking-mini` are its highest-scoring models in the SWE-bench Verified comparison.

safety_findings.text: Family-level safe-completions training applies across GPT-5 models and aims to keep output safe while preserving helpfulness on ambiguous and dual-use prompts.
Appendix safety tables show high `not_unsafe` scores for `gpt-5-thinking-mini`, with personal-data lower than most other standard categories.
StrongReject scores for `gpt-5-thinking-mini` are high but not perfect across illicit, violence, abuse/disinformation/hate, and sexual-content prompt groups.
Family-level biological safeguards cover `gpt-5-thinking-mini` production traffic with model training, two-tier monitoring, and account-level enforcement.
Cyber Range results improve for mini, but OpenAI says the GPT-5 model series does not meet the High cyber-risk threshold in this card.
OpenAI lists residual family-level biorisk concerns around policy gray areas, incremental information accumulation, trusted access, and API actor attribution.

limitations.text: The system card focuses on `gpt-5-thinking` and `gpt-5-main`, with mini-specific results limited to selected sections and the appendix.
No dedicated GPT-5 mini card exists, so this digest relies on the card's `gpt-5-thinking-mini` evidence and the family-scope statement.
Larger sibling results for `gpt-5-thinking`, `gpt-5-main`, and `gpt-5-thinking-pro` should not be attributed to GPT-5 mini.
Production Benchmark prompts are intentionally harder than standard content-safety tests and should not be read as normal production rates.
Cyber Range is sensitive to hints and setup; OpenAI says the mini model's improvement still does not establish significant cyber risk.
HealthBench results do not make the model a medical professional or a disease diagnosis or treatment tool.
Family-level biological monitoring prioritizes recall, so safe use may sometimes be blocked.

practical_implications.text: Use GPT-5 mini for routine coding, targeted edits, and explanations where speed and scope matter more than maximum reasoning depth.
Use only mini-specific results when comparing the model; avoid importing GPT-5 Thinking or GPT-5 main scores.
Verify factual claims and domain-specific advice despite the improved mini results on several benchmarks.
Inspect untrusted issue text, logs, web content, and tool output before letting it steer generated code.
Run tests and review diffs for generated code, especially for broad changes or hidden assumptions.

coverage_notes: This digest uses the GPT-5 System Card's family-scope statement, `gpt-5-thinking-mini` benchmark results, appendix safety tables, and family-level biological safeguards. Sibling-model results are excluded unless the card specifically names `gpt-5-thinking-mini`.
